The one entry here that is a DELIBERATE reduction rather than an addition, and it is allowlisted on a different invariant. This is the full-screen analysis veil: it carries `.isModal` and an indeterminate `ProgressView`, and VoiceOver re-reads a modal's element every time focus returns to it. Its fragments are a header plus 'Reading what you caught…' — two sentences that say the same thing twice and re-speak on every focus event during a multi-second wait. One short sentence naming the blocking operation is the correct utterance for a modal veil. The `.accessibilityIdentifier("captureAnalyzing")` on the next line is what the UI suites query, so shortening the label broke nothing.

Same invariant as the saved-recipe row: adds the row KIND to fragments that are a name plus a macro triple and are otherwise indistinguishable from a saved recipe. NOTE: FoodView.swift is fenced this round — re-verify at reconciliation.

Adds the CAPTION-TO-VALUE relation. The fragments are a slot caption and a value drawn one above the other; `.combine` speaks them as two unlinked items in one breath, and the widget slot rows stack several of them, so a user hears four captions and four values with no way to pair them. The colon is what carries the pairing in speech. `Text(slot)` rather than `slot` is deliberate and commented at the site: a `LocalizedStringKey` cannot be interpolated into another `LocalizedStringKey`, but a `Text` carries its own lookup.

Adds the UNIT and the of-relation, neither of which is ever drawn. The macro rows render a name, a filled bar and two numerals; the word 'grams' appears nowhere on screen and 'of' is expressed purely by the bar's geometry, so `.combine` yields 'Protein 40 120'. Covers both macro rows (the compact and the AX-size variant of the same helper) — they are the same code shape, deliberately, so one entry covering two hits is the honest pin rather than two copies of one reason.

Adds the AUTHOR. `.combine` gathers a chat bubble's fragments, which are a sender-name caption plus the message text for an INCOMING message and the message text ALONE for an outgoing one — the name caption is drawn only under `if !message.isOutgoing` (:103). So an outgoing bubble combines to the bare sentence with nothing saying who sent it; authorship is carried purely by right-alignment and the terracotta tint, and neither of those is speech. The label restores it ('You: …') and supplies the speaker-to-utterance colon on the incoming branch. This site was invisible to the wall until the 2026-08-23 A1 hardening: `.accessibilityIdentifier("session.chat.message")` sits BETWEEN `.combine` and the label, and the old rule inspected only the immediately-next code line — this is the review's planted evasion #3 (one interleaved modifier) occurring naturally in shipping code, and surfacing it is the hardening working. NOTE: SessionChatPanel.swift is NOT part of this round's diff. The entry pins a PRE-EXISTING shape the tightened rule newly reaches, not a line this batch wrote. The reported text is the bare `.accessibilityLabel(` because the argument wraps to the following lines; this file contains exactly one `.combine` chain, so the entry cannot drift onto a second site.

Adds the SENTENCE. The tile's fragments are a bare count numeral and a shelf label ('12', 'journal shelf'); `row.headline` is the warm sentence the milestone card is actually about ('You've written 12 journal moments.'). SEPARATE OPEN DEFECT, recorded here rather than hidden: `MilestoneRow.headline` is a plain `String` built from unlocalized English literals in `MilestonesView.headline(kind:count:)`, and it is ALSO rendered visually as `Text(row.headline)` at :199 — so this is display copy frozen in English, not merely an accessibility label. The A1 invariant above holds regardless of that; the localization fix (a plural-aware catalog fork of ~10 switch arms) is named as a residual in the batch report and does not belong in this file's entry.

NOT a photograph or a rendered bitmap, which are what A6 protects. `KeyboardDoneGlyph.image()` is an `.alwaysTemplate` copy of the SF Symbol `checkmark.circle.fill`: a template image has no colours of its own and is drawn entirely in the button's tint (moss), so it is interface ink, the same thing as the `Image(systemName:)` glyphs this rule never matches (the Swift port's fixture says why: 'Smart Invert is supposed to invert UI chrome'). It passes through `Image(uiImage:)` for one reason, commented at the site: the keyboard bar draws the button as a native image item and names it after its image alone, so the UIImage has to carry the localized 'Done' label — an `Image(systemName:)` there was read as 'selected'. `.accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors()` would be the defect here rather than the fix: its whole effect is to hold a view at its un-inverted colours, which here means a moss checkmark on a bar that has inverted under it, a glyph that no longer follows the interface it belongs to. Measured 2026-10-01 (iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 26.5, Smart Invert on, screens captured by XCUITest): a progress photo that carries the opt-out is captured as its colour negative — the counter-inversion that lets the display's inversion restore it — while this glyph, its bar and the keyboard are captured untouched, pixel for pixel the same as with Smart Invert off, so they invert together. The invariant is the template rendering mode inside `KeyboardDoneGlyph.image()`, and its doc comment says so: if that image ever carries colours of its own, delete this entry and decide the site against A6 again. `line_contains` names the glyph, so the entry cannot drift onto `PolaroidTile`'s photograph earlier in the same file, which carries its opt-out.

A DIVIDER between sections of the privacy policy, measuring ~1.70:1 against the page. It is decoration, not information: every section it separates opens with its own heading (and VoiceOver never reaches a Divider), so WCAG 1.4.11 does not ask it to contrast. Raising it to 3:1 would make the policy's rules darker than its body text's quietest ink without telling anyone anything.

MacroInputRow's inline gram editor never shows a prompt, so there is no placeholder ink to fix. The field exists only while `isEditing` is true, and the tap that sets it first writes the current value into `textValue` (`MacroGramEntry.display(grams)`), so the field opens prefilled; clearing it and leaving commits nothing and closes the field (`commit()` ends editing whether or not the text parses). Its title is empty because the row's own bark label beside it names the value.
